title: Polynomial-time trajectory output
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $C,e,c,A,d$ be natural numbers. The function that sends each Boolean word $x$ to the serialized trajectory prefix for $M$ on the all-false word of length $m=|x|+C(|x|+1)^e$, through horizon $T=c(A(m+1)^d+1)^2$ and with $T+1$ rows, is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: For every source machine and parameters $C, e, c, A, d$, the function sending an instance $x$ to the inclusive serialized trajectory over the all-false reference input of length $m = |x| + C(|x|+1)^e$ at horizon $T = c(A(m+1)^d+1)^2$, with $T+1$ rows, is polynomial-time computable; the output is produced by the actual recorder, not read off a prepared configuration.
